text: For a Hill function f(X) = Xⁿ/(Kⁿ+Xⁿ) describing transcriptional activation, what does a Hill coefficient of n = 1 correspond to?
choices: A hyperbolic response equivalent to Michaelis-Menten saturation
No dependence of the response on X at all
explanation: With n = 1, the Hill function reduces to X/(K+X), a hyperbolic saturation curve mathematically identical in form to Michaelis-Menten kinetics. A step-function switch instead requires n → ∞, a sigmoidal ultrasensitive response requires n > 1, and 'no dependence on X' is not true for any finite positive n, since the function still increases monotonically with X.
